Title: Process schema referential integrity hardening
Purpose: Add the missing definition-child and runtime foreign keys, choose delete behaviors intentionally, and stop relying on ordered delete code as the primary integrity mechanism.
Deliverables: Explicit FK mappings for the remaining Process definition-child and runtime tables.
Provider migrations for SQLite and PostgreSQL reflecting the new FK graph.
A short written delete-behavior map explaining which links cascade, restrict, or set-null and why.
Integration tests proving the DB rejects representative orphan rows and invalid references.
ReviewQuestions: Does the DB now reject representative orphan definition-child and runtime rows?
Are delete behaviors explicit and documented instead of incidental?
Did FK hardening preserve differential save and delete behavior?
CorrectiveOnFailure: If FK hardening causes save-cycle failures, do not quietly remove the FK plan. Open the DB-integrity corrective playbook and redesign the save ordering or ownership model first.
